fullPassage:
Letters to Nature

Dear Tree,
Whenever I walk past you, your beautiful leaves bring a smile to my face. Whenever I stop in front of you and take a deep breath of fresh air, I appreciate the oxygen that you produce. Without you and all your friends, we humans wouldn't be able to get enough oxygen. By the way, I noticed that a family of birds has made a nest in your branches. It's so kind of you to provide them with a home. I hope that more people realize how important you and all the other trees are to the environment. Have a nice day!

Believe it or not, trees in Melbourne, Australia receive emails like this all the time. How is it possible that trees have email addresses? And why are people sending them messages?

The story behind these emails begins with Melbourne's Urban Forest Strategy plan, a response to Australia's millennium drought. This drought lasted from the late 1990s to 2010. By the time it ended, 40 percent of the city's 77,000 trees were in a state of declining health. Furthermore, the overall number of trees was decreasing.

As a result, the amount of shade provided by trees within the city, also known as canopy cover, decreased. The loss of canopy cover is a major threat to urban environments because it raises temperatures. Higher temperatures in cities can be dangerous for residents, as they increase the risk of heat exhaustion. They also lead to a rise in the use of air conditioning. This speeds up climate change by increasing energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions.

Something had to be done to deal with the loss of Melbourne's trees. In 2012, the city government announced its Urban Forest Strategy plan. It set the ambitious goal of planting more than 3,000 trees every year for the next twenty years. The plan also involved the creation of an online map called the Urban Forest Visual.

This interactive map shows the location of every single tree in the city's parks and along its roads. It uses colors and symbols to indicate each tree's age and genus. Also, users can click on a tree to find out its species and even send it an email. At first, the "Email this tree" function had a specific purpose. It was designed to allow people to easily inform council workers about trees that were damaged or in poor health.

After the map was posted online, something unexpected happened. The trees started receiving thousands of emails, but many of them were not reports about damage or poor health. Instead, they were love letters, poems, greetings, and messages expressing appreciation for the trees. One person wrote, "I love the way the light shines on your leaves and how your branches hang so low. It is almost like you are trying to hug me." The tree mail phenomenon quickly spread, and people all over the world started sending messages.

A message that was sent all the way from Russia said, "When I read about this wonderful project, I was inspired to write to you, even though I live thousands of miles away. Although we are separated by a great distance, we share the same planet and the same environment. Perhaps one day we will meet. Until then, I hope you can stay healthy and strong."

The global popularity of the tree mail phenomenon reminds us that we are all connected to nature, and we are all involved in building a more sustainable world. Without collective action from people across the globe, we would have little hope of saving our planet for future generations.

Locally, the tree mail phenomenon has inspired many Melbourne residents to offer their own ideas about building an environmentally friendly urban environment. Some have even volunteered to measure trees and monitor animals for nature programs in the city.

Meanwhile, the Urban Forest Strategy's tree planting project has remained on track, and canopy cover is predicted to increase from 23 percent in 2012 to 40 percent by the year 2040. Melbourne's urban forest strategy will help keep the city cool. It will also allow residents to interact with nature and engage in outdoor activities every day. As a result, residents will be happier and healthier as they move toward a greener future.

questions.passage: Whenever I walk past you, your beautiful leaves bring a smile to my face. Whenever I stop in front of you and take a deep (A)[breath / break] of fresh air, I (B)[appreciate / approach] the oxygen that you produce. Without you and all your friends, we humans wouldn't be able to get (C)[enough / rough] oxygen.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 깊은 숨을 들이마실 때마다 너가 만들어 내는 산소에 감사해. 너 없이는 충분한 산소를 얻을 수 없을 거야.
det.analysis: ✅ (A) breath: 'take a deep breath(깊은 숨을 쉬다)'는 관용 표현. break(휴식)는 문맥 부적합. ✅ (B) appreciate: 산소에 '감사하다'. approach(접근하다)는 의미 불일치. ✅ (C) enough: '충분한' 산소. rough(거친)는 산소를 수식하기에 부적합.
det.tip: take a deep breath: 깊은 숨을 쉬다. appreciate: 감사하다/진가를 알다.

questions.passage: This drought lasted from the late 1990s to 2010. By the time it ended, 40 percent of the city's 77,000 trees were in a state of (A)[declining / inclining] health. Furthermore, the overall number of trees was (B)[decreasing / increasing]. As a result, the amount of shade provided by trees within the city, also known as canopy cover, (C)[decreased / improved].
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 나무의 40%가 건강이 나빠지는 상태에 있었다. 나무 수도 감소하고 있었다. 그 결과 그늘의 양이 감소했다.
det.analysis: ✅ (A) declining: 건강이 '감소하는/나빠지는' 상태. inclining(기우는)은 건강 상태와 어울리지 않음. ✅ (B) decreasing: 나무 수가 '감소'하고 있었다. increasing(증가)은 가뭄 상황과 모순. ✅ (C) decreased: 그늘의 양이 '감소'했다. improved(개선되다)는 가뭄으로 인한 부정적 상황과 모순.
det.tip: declining health: 건강이 악화되는 상태. decline과 decrease는 모두 '줄다'이지만, decline은 질적 저하, decrease는 양적 감소.

questions.passage: In 2012, the city government announced its Urban Forest Strategy plan. It set the (A)[ambitious / ambiguous] goal of planting more than 3,000 trees every year. The plan also involved the creation of an online map called the Urban Forest Visual. This (B)[interactive / attractive] map shows the location of every single tree. It uses colors and symbols to (C)[indicate / imitate] each tree's age and genus.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 야심찬 목표를 설정했다. 이 대화형 지도는 나무의 위치를 보여준다. 나이와 속을 나타내기 위해 색상과 기호를 사용한다.
det.analysis: ✅ (A) ambitious: '야심찬' 목표. ambiguous(모호한)는 구체적 수치(3,000그루)와 모순. ✅ (B) interactive: 사용자가 클릭할 수 있는 '대화형' 지도. attractive(매력적인)는 기능 설명과 어울리지 않음. ✅ (C) indicate: 나이와 속을 '나타내다'. imitate(모방하다)는 지도 기능과 무관.
det.tip: ambitious(야심찬) vs ambiguous(모호한): 발음이 비슷하지만 의미가 완전히 다름. interactive: 상호작용하는, 대화형의.

questions.passage: Whenever I walk past you, your beautiful leaves bring a ①<u>smile</u> to my face. I appreciate the oxygen that you ②<u>produce</u>. I hope that more people ③<u>ignore</u> how important you and all the other trees are to the environment. It's so kind of you to ④<u>provide</u> them with a home.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 더 많은 사람들이 나무가 환경에 얼마나 중요한지 깨닫기를 바란다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①smile(미소): 아름다운 잎이 미소를 짓게 한다. 원문 그대로. ✅ ②produce(생산하다): 산소를 '생산하다'. 원문 그대로. ✅ ③able(~할 수 있는): 'be able to get'. 원문 그대로. ❌ ④ignore(무시하다): 원문은 realize(깨닫다). 나무의 중요성을 더 많은 사람들이 '깨닫기를' 바라는 맥락. ignore는 정반대 의미.
det.tip: realize(깨닫다) ↔ ignore(무시하다). 환경 보호 맥락에서 중요성을 '깨닫다'가 자연스러움.

questions.passage: The loss of canopy cover is a major ①<u>threat</u> to urban environments because it raises temperatures. Higher temperatures in cities can be ②<u>dangerous</u> for residents, as they increase the ③<u>risk</u> of heat exhaustion. They also lead to a rise in the use of air conditioning. This speeds up climate change by ④<u>decreasing</u> energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이는 에너지 소비와 온실가스 배출물을 증가시킴으로써 기후변화를 가속화한다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①threat(위협): 임관 피복도 줄어듦은 도시 환경에 '위협'. 원문 그대로. ✅ ②dangerous(위험한): 높은 기온은 주민에게 '위험하다'. 원문 그대로. ✅ ③risk(위험): 열사병의 '위험'을 높인다. 원문 그대로. ❌ ④decreasing(감소시키는): 원문은 increasing(증가시키는). 에너지 소비와 온실가스 배출이 '증가'해서 기후변화가 가속화되므로 decreasing은 정반대.
det.tip: increasing(증가시키는) ↔ decreasing(감소시키는). 에어컨 사용 증가 → 에너지 소비 '증가' → 기후변화 가속화.

questions.passage: The global popularity of the tree mail phenomenon ①<u>reminds</u> us that we are all connected to nature, and we are all involved in building a more ②<u>sustainable</u> world. Without collective action from people across the globe, we would have ③<u>little</u> hope of saving our planet for future generations. Locally, the tree mail phenomenon has ④<u>discouraged</u> many Melbourne residents to offer their own ideas about building an environmentally friendly urban environment.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 나무 이메일 현상은 많은 멜버른 주민들이 아이디어를 제안하도록 고무했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ①reminds(일깨워 준다): 자연과 연결되어 있다는 것을 '일깨워 준다'. 원문 그대로. ✅ ②sustainable(지속 가능한): 보다 '지속 가능한' 세상. 원문 그대로. ✅ ③little(거의 없는): 집단 행동 없이는 희망이 '거의 없을' 것. 원문 그대로. ❌ ④discouraged(낙담시켰다): 원문은 inspired(고무했다). 주민들이 아이디어를 '제안하도록' 했으므로 긍정적 의미가 맞음. discouraged는 정반대.
det.tip: inspire(고무하다) ↔ discourage(낙담시키다). 긍정적 결과(아이디어 제안)로 이어졌으므로 inspire가 적절.

questions.passage: Whenever I walk past you, your beautiful leaves bring a smile to my face. Whenever I stop in front of you and take a deep breath of fresh air, I appreciate the oxygen that you produce. Without you and all your friends, we humans wouldn't be able to get enough oxygen. By the way, I noticed that a family of birds has made a __________ in your branches. It's so kind of you to provide them with a home.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 한 새 가족이 너의 가지에 둥지를 틀었다.
det.analysis: ✅ nest(둥지): 새 가족이 가지에 '둥지'를 만들었다. 'made a nest'는 원문 표현. ✗ leaf(잎): 새가 잎을 만드는 것은 부자연스러움. ✗ root(뿌리): 가지에 뿌리를 만드는 것은 불가. ✗ seed(씨앗): 새가 씨앗을 만드는 것은 부적절.
det.tip: make a nest: 둥지를 틀다. 새와 관련된 핵심 표현.

questions.passage: Believe it or not, trees in Melbourne, Australia receive emails like this all the time. How is it possible that trees have email addresses? And why are people sending them messages? The story behind these emails begins with Melbourne's Urban Forest Strategy plan, a __________ to Australia's millennium drought. This drought lasted from the late 1990s to 2010.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 호주의 밀레니엄 가뭄에 대한 대응인, 멜버른의 도시숲 전략 계획.
det.analysis: ✅ response(대응): 가뭄에 대한 '대응'으로서의 전략. 'a response to'는 원문 표현. ✗ alternative(대안): '대안'이라면 'an alternative to'이나 가뭄 자체의 대안이라는 표현은 부자연스러움. ✗ obstacle(장애물): 전략이 장애물이라는 것은 의미상 반대. ✗ donation(기부): 문맥과 전혀 관련 없음.
det.tip: a response to: ~에 대한 대응/반응. response는 문제 상황에 대한 조치나 반응을 뜻함.

questions.passage: This interactive map shows the location of every single tree in the city's parks and along its roads. It uses colors and symbols to indicate each tree's age and genus. Also, users can click on a tree to find out its species and even send it an email. At first, the "Email this tree" function had a specific purpose. It was designed to allow people to easily __________ council workers about trees that were damaged or in poor health.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 손상되거나 건강이 좋지 않은 나무들에 관해 의회 직원들에게 쉽게 알려주도록 고안되었다.
det.analysis: ✅ inform(알려주다): 'inform council workers about ~'는 원문 그대로. 손상된 나무를 '보고'하는 목적. ✗ prevent(예방하다): 'prevent workers about'은 비문법적. ✗ replace(교체하다): 직원을 교체한다는 의미로 문맥 불일치. ✗ convince(설득하다): 보고 기능의 목적과 어울리지 않음.
det.tip: inform A about B: A에게 B에 관해 알리다. '정보 전달'의 핵심 동사.

questions.passage: As a result, the amount of shade provided by trees within the city, also known as canopy cover, decreased. The loss of canopy cover is a major <u>threat</u> to urban environments because it raises temperatures. Higher temperatures in cities can be dangerous for residents, as they increase the risk of heat exhaustion. They also lead to a rise in the use of air conditioning. This speeds up climate change by increasing energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 단어와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 임관 피복도의 줄어듦은 도시 환경에 주요한 위협이다.
det.analysis: ✅ danger(위험): threat와 danger는 모두 '위험/위협'의 의미. ✗ benefit(이익): 정반대 의미. ✗ tradition(전통): 무관. ✗ solution(해결책): 위협이 아닌 해결책은 반대 맥락.
det.tip: threat = danger: 위험, 위협. a threat to: ~에 대한 위협.

questions.passage: Something had to be done to deal with the loss of Melbourne's trees. In 2012, the city government announced its Urban Forest Strategy plan. It set the <u>ambitious</u> goal of planting more than 3,000 trees every year for the next twenty years. The plan also involved the creation of an online map called the Urban Forest Visual. This interactive map shows the location of every single tree in the city's parks and along its roads.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 단어와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 매년 3,000그루가 넘는 나무를 심는 야심찬 목표를 설정했다.
det.analysis: ✅ challenging(도전적인): ambitious는 '야심찬, 대담한'으로 높은 목표를 뜻함. challenging도 '도전적인, 어려운' 의미로 유사. ✗ modest(겸손한, 적당한): ambitious와 반대. ✗ realistic(현실적인): 야심찬 목표는 현실적이기보다 대담한 것. ✗ ordinary(평범한): ambitious와 반대.
det.tip: ambitious: 야심찬, 대담한. 높은 목표나 큰 계획에 사용. ≈ challenging, daring.

questions.passage: The global popularity of the tree mail phenomenon reminds us that we are all connected to nature, and we are all involved in building a more sustainable world. Without <u>collective</u> action from people across the globe, we would have little hope of saving our planet for future generations. Locally, the tree mail phenomenon has inspired many Melbourne residents to offer their own ideas about building an environmentally friendly urban environment. Some have even volunteered to measure trees and monitor animals for nature programs in the city.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 단어와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 전 세계 사람들로부터의 집단적인 행동이 없다면.
det.analysis: ✅ joint(공동의): collective와 joint는 모두 '함께하는, 공동의'라는 의미. ✗ individual(개인의): collective의 정반대. ✗ military(군사적): 문맥과 무관. ✗ political(정치적인): 환경 행동의 맥락과 직접 연결되지 않음.
det.tip: collective = joint: 집단적인, 공동의. collective action: 집단 행동.

questions.passage: After the map was posted online, something <u>unexpected</u> happened. The trees started receiving thousands of emails, but many of them were not reports about damage or poor health. Instead, they were love letters, poems, greetings, and messages expressing appreciation for the trees. One person wrote, "I love the way the light shines on your leaves and how your branches hang so low. It is almost like you are trying to hug me."
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 단어와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 지도가 온라인에 게재된 후, 예상 밖의 일이 일어났다.
det.analysis: ✅ predictable(예측 가능한): unexpected(예상 밖의)의 정반대. ✗ unusual(특이한): unexpected와 유사한 의미. ✗ surprising(놀라운): unexpected와 유사. ✗ remarkable(주목할 만한): 반대가 아닌 유사 뉘앙스.
det.tip: unexpected(예상 밖의) ↔ predictable(예측 가능한). un- 접두사가 '반대'를 만듦.

questions.passage: This drought lasted from the late 1990s to 2010. By the time it ended, 40 percent of the city's 77,000 trees were in a state of declining health. Furthermore, the overall number of trees was <u>decreasing</u>. As a result, the amount of shade provided by trees within the city, also known as canopy cover, decreased. The loss of canopy cover is a major threat to urban environments because it raises temperatures.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 단어와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 나무들의 전반적인 수가 감소하고 있었다.
det.analysis: ✅ expanding(확대되는): decreasing(감소하는)의 정반대. ✗ declining(감소하는): decreasing과 동의어. ✗ reducing(줄이는): decreasing과 유사. ✗ shrinking(줄어드는): decreasing과 유사.
det.tip: decreasing(감소하는) ↔ expanding(확대되는)/increasing(증가하는). 오답 3개가 모두 유의어이므로 소거법 활용.

questions.passage: Locally, the tree mail phenomenon has inspired many Melbourne residents to <u>offer</u> their own ideas about building an environmentally friendly urban environment. Some have even volunteered to measure trees and monitor animals for nature programs in the city. Meanwhile, the Urban Forest Strategy's tree planting project has remained on track, and canopy cover is predicted to increase from 23 percent in 2012 to 40 percent by the year 2040. Melbourne's urban forest strategy will help keep the city cool.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 offer가 이 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: to give something to someone as a gift
to suggest or propose an idea
to provide a service at a certain price
to express willingness to do something

det.korean: 많은 멜버른 주민들이 그들만의 생각들을 제안하도록 고무했다.
det.analysis: ✅ ②to suggest or propose an idea(아이디어를 제안하다): ideas를 목적어로 취하여 '아이디어를 제안하다'의 의미. ✗ ①선물로 주다: ideas와 어울리지 않음. ✗ ③서비스를 제공하다: 가격 언급 없음. ✗ ④기꺼이 하다: offer to V 구문이 아님.
det.tip: offer는 다의어: ①제안하다 ②제공하다 ③내밀다. 'offer ideas'에서는 '제안하다'가 가장 적절.

questions.passage: Meanwhile, the Urban Forest Strategy's tree planting project has remained on track, and canopy cover is predicted to increase from 23 percent in 2012 to 40 percent by the year 2040.
questions.stem: 다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어를 글에서 찾으면? "to say that something will happen in the future based on evidence"

det.korean: 임관 피복도는 2040년까지 40퍼센트로 늘어날 것으로 예상된다.
det.analysis: ✅ predicted(예상되다): '증거에 기반하여 미래에 일어날 일을 말하다'는 predict의 정의. ✗ remained(남아있다): 상태 유지를 뜻함. ✗ increased(증가하다): 양이 늘어나는 것. ✗ involved(포함하다): 관련시키다의 의미.
det.tip: predict: 예측하다. evidence(증거)에 기반한 예측이라는 점이 guess(추측)와의 차이.

questions.passage: Higher temperatures in cities can be dangerous for residents, as they increase the risk of heat exhaustion. They also lead to a rise in the use of air conditioning. This speeds up climate change by increasing energy __________ and greenhouse gas emissions.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. [consume]

det.korean: 에너지 소비와 온실가스 배출물을 증가시킴으로써.
det.analysis: consume(동사: 소비하다) → consumption(명사: 소비). energy와 함께 쓰여 '에너지 소비'를 뜻하며, 빈칸 앞 energy가 형용사처럼 명사를 수식하는 구조.
det.tip: consume(v. 소비하다) → consumption(n. 소비) → consumer(n. 소비자). 동사→명사 변환 시 -tion 접미사 활용.

questions.passage: It will also allow residents to interact with nature and engage in outdoor activities every day. As a result, residents will be happier and __________ as they move toward a greener future.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. [health]

det.korean: 주민들은 더 건강해질 것이다.
det.analysis: health(명사: 건강) → healthy(형용사: 건강한) → healthier(비교급: 더 건강한). happier와 and로 병렬 연결되므로 같은 비교급 형태가 필요.
det.tip: happier and healthier: 비교급 병렬 구조. -y로 끝나는 형용사의 비교급은 -ier.

questions.passage: Whenever I walk past you, your beautiful leaves bring a smile to my face. Without you and all your friends, we humans wouldn't be able to get enough oxygen. By the way, I noticed that a family of birds has made a nest in your branches. It's so kind of you to provide them with a home. I hope that more people realize how important you and all the other trees are to the __________. Have a nice day!
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 너와 다른 모든 나무들이 환경에 얼마나 중요한지.
det.analysis: ✅ environment(환경): 나무가 중요한 대상은 '환경'. 원문 그대로. ✗ economy(경제): 나무 편지의 맥락과 무관. ✗ technology(기술): 자연과 관련 없음. ✗ community(공동체): 가능하지만 원문과 불일치.
det.tip: environment: 환경. 나무와 자연의 중요성을 말하는 맥락에서 핵심 단어.

questions.passage: Locally, the tree mail phenomenon has inspired many Melbourne residents to offer their own ideas about building an environmentally friendly urban environment. Some have even __________ to measure trees and monitor animals for nature programs in the city. Meanwhile, the Urban Forest Strategy's tree planting project has remained on track. Canopy cover is predicted to increase from 23 percent in 2012 to 40 percent by the year 2040. Melbourne's urban forest strategy will help keep the city cool.
questions.stem: 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 일부는 심지어 나무를 측정하고 동물을 추적 관찰하는 일을 자원하기까지 했다.
det.analysis: ✅ volunteered(자원했다): 자발적으로 자연 프로그램에 참여했다는 맥락. 원문 그대로. ✗ refused(거절했다): 자발적 참여와 정반대. ✗ hesitated(주저했다): 'even'이 강조하는 적극성과 모순. ✗ struggled(분투했다): 어려움을 겪었다는 의미로 문맥 불일치.
det.tip: volunteer to V: 자원하여 ~하다. 'even volunteered'에서 even은 놀라운 적극성을 강조.
